html:
The Second Boer War was a war of 1899 to 1902 between the British Empire and the two Boer republics of southern Africa, the Transvaal and the Orange Free State. Britain won, but at a cost that shocked the empire.

The cause was gold. The Witwatersrand gold rush from 1886 made the Transvaal rich and filled it with foreign miners, the Uitlanders, whom President Paul Kruger refused the vote. Mining magnates and Cecil Rhodes backed the failed Jameson Raid of 1895 to overthrow him. Talks broke down, and the Boers struck first in October 1899.

  • The Boers besieged Ladysmith in Natal, Kimberley and Mafeking, and beat British armies in "Black Week" in December 1899. Sol Plaatje kept a diary of the siege of Mafeking.
  • Reinforced from across the empire, the British took Bloemfontein and Pretoria in 1900.
  • The Boers then fought on as mounted guerrillas for two more years.

To end the guerrilla war, the British burned farms and moved Boer women and children and Black Africans into concentration camps. Disease killed over 26,000 Boers in the camps, most of them children, and many thousands of Black Africans. Gandhi led an Indian ambulance corps for the British.

The Treaty of Vereeniging in 1902 made both republics British colonies. In 1910 they joined Natal and the Cape in the Union of South Africa, under a deal that left most Black South Africans without the vote.
sum: The Second Boer War was a war of 1899 to 1902 between the British Empire and the two Boer republics of southern Africa, the Transvaal and the Orange Free State. Britain won, but at a cost that shocked the empire.
